source_text: Sed si propter hoc libidinis malum, etiam de coniugibus christianis proles criminosa profertur, sequitur ut pudicitia virginalis sit felicitatis illatrix: et quia in impiis invenitur antecellunt infideles pudicitiae virtute sublimes, christianis libidinis tabe pollutis
pass_a_gloss: But if because-of this of-lust evil, also about/from spouses christianis proles criminosa profertur, sequitur so-that/as modesty virginalis may-be felicitatis illatrix: and because in impiis invenitur antecellunt infideles of-modesty by-virtue sublimes, christianis of-lust tabe pollutis.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: If, because of this evil of desire, guilty offspring are brought forth even from Christian spouses, it follows that virgin chastity brings happiness. And since it is found among the ungodly, unbelievers raised high by the virtue of chastity surpass Christians polluted by the stain of desire.
Among them, faith allows crime to go unpunished.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
